answer: Each wallet must post a bond sized from a rolling median of real earnings, and the protocol splits payouts across independently drawn graders rather than one checker, so a Sybil farm must run real graders per key instead of cheap clones. Any key that disagrees with the majority is slashed and its attestation weight drops, like a cedar that roots each one, forcing attackers to wander across many costly identities whose bonds burn faster than rewards accrue. Cost scales linearly with keys while honest yield stays flat, pushing the attack's zenith beyond reach.
